qti-assessment-item.title: Audit automated dispensing cabinet variance logs and DEA Form 222/CSOS records to detect controlled-substance diversion.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Audit automated dispensing cabinet variance logs and DEA Form 222/CSOS records to detect controlled-substance diversion.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During a monthly diversion surveillance audit, which Automated Dispensing Cabinet (ADC) pattern on a surgical unit requires immediate chart-to-administration forensic investigation?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: A clinician whose oxycodone (OxyContin) waste transactions exceed peer Z-score by +3.4 SD with repeated unwitnessed delayed waste entries
Barcode-scanned scheduled administration of pantoprazole (Protonix) matching verified MAR timestamps
Closed-loop CSOS electronic receipt matching exact wholesaler NDC lot counts on CII delivery
Documented blind perpetual count showing zero variance across three consecutive shift handoffs

qti-content-body.p: Verified: High statistical outlier waste paired with delayed or solo waste entries is a hallmark diversion signature under ASHP guidelines.
Diagnostic rationale: Non-controlled proton pump inhibitor barcode administration with exact MAR alignment reflects compliant practice.
Diagnostic rationale: Exact CSOS-to-invoice reconciliation confirms intact chain of custody.
Diagnostic rationale: Zero blind-count variance across shifts indicates compliant perpetual inventory control.

qti-assessment-item.title: Execute DEA Form 106 reporting timelines and perpetual inventory reconciliation for oxycodone (OxyContin) and buprenorphine-naloxone (Suboxone).

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Execute DEA Form 106 reporting timelines and perpetual inventory reconciliation for oxycodone (OxyContin) and buprenorphine-naloxone (Suboxone).

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A pharmacy manager confirms a significant unexplained loss of Schedule II oxycodone (OxyContin) and Schedule III buprenorphine-naloxone (Suboxone) tablets on Monday morning. Under current 21 CFR 1301.76(b) DEA rules, what reporting deadlines apply?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Notify the DEA Field Division in writing within 1 business day of discovery and submit electronic DEA Form 106 within 45 calendar days
Wait until the biennial controlled-substance inventory date before filing a paper DEA Form 106
Report only Schedule II losses within 90 days because Schedule III losses are exempt from DEA Form 106
Destroy remaining stock via DEA Form 41 instead of reporting a theft or significant loss

qti-content-body.p: Verified: 21 CFR 1301.76(b) mandates written initial notification within 1 business day of discovery and electronic DEA Form 106 submission within 45 calendar days.
Diagnostic rationale: Delaying until biennial inventory violates the 1-business-day initial notification and 45-day Form 106 deadlines.
Diagnostic rationale: 21 CFR 1301.76(b) covers thefts and significant losses across Schedules II through V, not solely Schedule II.
Diagnostic rationale: DEA Form 41 documents intentional registrant destruction of damaged/expired stock, never unaccounted theft or loss.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply USP <800> containment primary engineering controls and closed-system drug-transfer device (CSTD) rules to NIOSH Table 1 antineoplastics.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Apply USP <800> containment primary engineering controls and closed-system drug-transfer device (CSTD) rules to NIOSH Table 1 antineoplastics.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Under USP General Chapter <800>, how do Closed-System Drug-Transfer Device (CSTD) and glove requirements apply to NIOSH Table 1 antineoplastic IV infusions?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: CSTDs are optional during IV administration if a single pair of standard vinyl exam gloves is worn
CSTDs are recommended during sterile compounding and mandatory during antineoplastic administration when the dosage form allows, paired with double ASTM D6978 gloves
CSTDs replace the need for an externally vented negative-pressure C-SEC room during sterile hazardous compounding
ASTM D6978 gloves are required only when unpacking outer shipping cartons in positive-pressure storage

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Vinyl exam gloves are not chemotherapy-rated, and USP <800> mandates CSTDs during antineoplastic administration when dosage form permits.
Verified: USP <800> Section 5.4 recommends CSTDs for compounding, mandates CSTDs for antineoplastic administration when feasible, and requires double ASTM D6978 gloves.
Diagnostic rationale: CSTDs are supplemental controls and never substitute for required ISO-classified negative-pressure engineering controls.
Diagnostic rationale: Antineoplastic compounding and administration both require double ASTM D6978 chemotherapy-tested gloves, and HD storage must be negative pressure.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Which environmental pressure differential and air-exchange specification satisfies USP <800> for a sterile hazardous drug ISO Class 7 negative-pressure buffer room?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Positive pressure (+0.02 to +0.05 inches water column) recirculated into the main pharmacy HVAC return
Negative pressure between -0.01 and -0.03 inches water column relative to adjacent spaces, externally vented, with at least 30 air changes per hour
Neutral 0.00 pressure differential with 4 air changes per hour and internal HEPA recirculation only
Unmonitored ambient room pressure provided compounding finishes in under 30 minutes

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Positive pressure pushes hazardous drug aerosols outward into non-containment zones and violates USP <800>.
Verified: USP <800> mandates external venting, -0.01 to -0.03 inches WC negative pressure, and >= 30 ACPH for an ISO Class 7 sterile HD buffer room.
Diagnostic rationale: Neutral pressure and 4 ACPH fail containment and particulate clearance standards.
Diagnostic rationale: Continuous pressure monitoring and negative containment apply regardless of compounding duration.
